title: Arabic alphabets
intro: Recognise 28 letters and learn how their sounds differ.

title: Harakat
intro: Read short vowels: Zabar, Zer and Pesh.

lessons.title: Fatha / Zabar
lessons.body: A small stroke above gives a short a sound: ba.
lessons.question: Which mark is written above a letter?

lessons.title: Kasra / Zer
lessons.body: A small stroke below gives a short i sound: bi.
lessons.question: Which mark is written below?

lessons.title: Damma / Pesh
lessons.body: A small curl above gives a short u sound: bu. Keep vowels short.
lessons.question: Which mark gives short u?

title: Joining Arabic letters
intro: Read from right to left and recognise contextual forms.

lessons.title: Four forms
lessons.body: A joining letter can have isolated, initial, medial and final forms. Position changes shape, not identity.
lessons.question: Does a contextual shape change the letter identity?

lessons.title: One-way joining
lessons.example: ا د ذ ر ز و
lessons.body: These six letters do not connect to the next letter on their left. A preceding letter on the right may connect to them.
lessons.question: Which letter does not join to the next on its left?

lessons.title: Joined practice
lessons.body: Track each consonant and its vowel from right to left. The second example is kataba. Ask a teacher to check your reading.
lessons.question: Arabic is read in which direction?

title: Noorani Qaida basics
intro: Build reading skills with marks and short combinations.

lessons.title: Sukoon
lessons.body: Sukoon indicates no vowel after a consonant. Practise in a syllable with your teacher.
lessons.question: Sukoon means:

lessons.title: Shaddah / Tashdeed
lessons.body: Shaddah doubles a consonant: the first part is without a vowel and the second carries a vowel.
lessons.question: Shaddah indicates:

lessons.title: Tanween
lessons.body: Two vowel marks add a final n sound when connecting. Stopping rules differ.
lessons.question: Tanween adds which sound in connected reading?

lessons.title: Madd
lessons.body: Long aa, ee and oo use suitable vowel letters. Basic natural madd is two counts; other madd rules depend on context.
lessons.question: Basic natural madd lasts:

title: Tajweed foundations
intro: A reading introduction; practical recitation needs a qualified teacher.

lessons.title: Makharij and letter weight
lessons.body: Makharij are articulation points. Heavy letters are خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ. Do not make every letter heavy.
lessons.question: Are qaaf and kaaf identical?

lessons.title: Qalqalah
lessons.body: When sakin, these letters have a controlled release or echo. Do not add a full vowel.
lessons.question: Should you add a full vowel in qalqalah?

lessons.title: Ghunnah
lessons.body: Noon and meem with shaddah have a nasal sound held for two counts in standard beginner teaching.
lessons.question: Ghunnah uses:

lessons.title: Noon sakinah and tanween
lessons.body: Izhar: clear before ء ه ع ح غ خ. Idgham: merging before ي ر م ل و ن, with details for nasalisation. Iqlab: conversion before ب. Ikhfa: concealment before the remaining 15 letters. Apply only with guided examples.
lessons.question: Iqlab occurs before:

lessons.title: Meem sakinah
lessons.body: Before ب: ikhfa shafawi. Before م: idgham shafawi. Before other letters: izhar shafawi. Practise with a teacher.
lessons.question: Meem sakinah before meem uses:

lessons.title: Madd and stopping signs
lessons.body: Madd length depends on its cause and recitation method. Common stop signs: م indicates a required stop; لا indicates do not stop; ج permits a stop. Meaning and breath also matter.
lessons.question: Which sign commonly permits a stop?
